channel.title: Day & Night Services — Life Insurance
channel.description: Honest, no-pressure life insurance education from Greg Jimenez, independent broker.

item.title: Your 401k is not life insurance
item.description:
One builds money for a retirement you get to see. The other replaces your income for the people who would still have bills after you are gone. Two different problems.
If no one depends on your paycheck, you may genuinely not need it. If someone would have to change their whole life without your income, it is worth a 15-minute honest conversation.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: The day you hold your first baby
item.description:
That is the moment life insurance actually starts to matter. Not because anything will happen, but because if it did, they would still be okay.
It usually costs less than people guess. A lot less.

item.title: You just bought the house. Now what protects it?
item.description:
A mortgage is a promise that outlives a paycheck. If the income that covers it stops, the house should not be the thing your family loses.
A term policy sized to the loan is often the simplest, cheapest answer. No pressure to overbuy — just enough to keep them in the home.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Final expense is not about you
item.description:
It is about not leaving the bill to them. A funeral runs thousands of dollars, and it lands on your family in the hardest week of their lives.
A small policy covers it so they can grieve instead of scramble. Many of these skip the medical exam entirely.

item.title: "I think I'm already covered through work"
item.description:
Maybe you are. But work coverage usually ends the day the job does, and it is often one year of salary — not what a family actually needs.
It is worth knowing what you truly have before you count on it. I will read your current coverage with you, no charge.

item.title: Term vs. whole life, in plain English
item.description:
Term is renting protection for the years your family needs it most — cheap, simple, expires. Whole life is owning it for life and builds cash value — costs more.
Neither is 'better.' The right one depends on who depends on you and for how long. That is the whole conversation.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Nobody depends on your income? You may not need it
item.description:
I said it. If you are single with no kids and no one co-signed your debts, a big policy may be a waste of money right now.
I would rather tell you that for free than sell you something you do not need. When life changes, so does the answer.

item.title: A health scare makes this harder, not impossible
item.description:
Coverage is easiest to get while you are healthy — that is just the honest truth. But even with conditions, there are options, including plans with no medical exam.
Do not assume you are uninsurable. Let's find out what you actually qualify for.

item.title: What life insurance really costs
item.description:
Most people guess three to five times too high. A healthy 35-year-old can often cover a family for the price of a couple of dinners out a month.
You will not know your number until someone runs it honestly. That part is free.

item.title: Changed jobs? Check two things
item.description:
First, your old 401k — it does not have to sit where you left it. Second, the life coverage you just lost when the job ended.
A rollover and a personal policy travel with you. The job does not have to own either one.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Who is the beneficiary on your policy?
item.description:
If it still names an ex, an estate, or a minor with no trust, the money can land in the wrong hands or get stuck in probate.
It takes ten minutes to check and fix. Most people have never looked since the day they signed.
Free guide, no email: dayandnightsservices.com Education, not financial or tax advice. Greg Jimenez — Independent Broker — CA Lic 4423937

item.title: Business owners: what happens to it without you?
item.description:
If the business depends on you, so does everyone it employs and every loan it carries. Life coverage can keep the doors open and buy your partners time.
This is not a pitch — it is a plan every owner should at least have looked at once.

item.title: An honest word on "index" policies
item.description:
You will hear a lot of hype about tax-advantaged growth inside life insurance. Some of it is real; a lot of it is oversold.
I will walk you through where it fits and where it does not — no illustration promising a number nobody can guarantee. Straight talk only.

item.title: The best time to set this up was before you needed it
item.description:
Nobody plans on the hard day. The whole point of doing this now is that they are covered before anything is wrong.
Fifteen minutes, honest answers, zero pressure. If you do not need it, I will say so.
